title: HybridTier: an Adaptive and Lightweight CXL-Memory Tiering System
problem: CXL-based memory tiering systems must efficiently migrate pages between fast DRAM and slow CXL memory, but existing tiering systems fail to adapt to dynamically shifting hotness distributions and incur excessive memory and cache overhead from tracking metadata. Prior approaches use either long-term frequency or short-term recency but not both simultaneously.
motivation: CXL memory expands capacity at lower cost but at 2-3x higher access latency, so effective page migration between DRAM and CXL tiers is critical for performance, yet the dynamic, skewed access patterns of modern workloads defeat static tracking policies.
method: HybridTier simultaneously tracks both long-term data access frequency and short-term access momentum to capture and adapt to shifting hotness distributions. To reduce memory overhead, it employs probabilistic access tracking with compact data structures that trade a small amount of tracking inaccuracy for significantly lower memory footprint. Cache overhead is minimized by organizing tracking metadata in data-locality-optimized lightweight structures that reduce cache misses during hotness lookups. Migration decisions combine both temporal signals for higher accuracy than either alone.
key_novelty: Simultaneous dual-signal tracking (long-term frequency plus short-term momentum) combined with probabilistic metadata to achieve high hotness accuracy at minimal memory and cache overhead in CXL tiering.
contributions: HybridTier: an adaptive CXL memory tiering system combining long-term frequency and short-term momentum tracking
Probabilistic access tracking that reduces metadata memory overhead by 2.0-7.8x vs. prior systems
Locality-optimized lightweight data structures reducing cache misses by 1.7-3.5x
Up to 91% (19% geomean) performance improvement over prior tiering systems

metrics.speedup: up to 91%, 19% geomean over prior tiering systems
metrics.other: 2.0-7.8x less memory overhead, 1.7-3.5x fewer cache misses vs. prior systems

baselines: prior CXL tiering systems (not named in abstract)
limitations: Small tracking inaccuracy introduced by probabilistic metadata has negligible but non-zero application performance impact; behavior on highly adversarial access patterns not discussed.
primary_theme: adaptive CXL memory tiering with dual-signal probabilistic tracking
